findings.claim: Immediate endpoint selection evidence is strongest for short-range pair kernels: pair_kernel_1.5 (endpoint_effects:9, integrated z 0.562, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_2.5 (endpoint_effects:10, z 0.631, q 2.2e-5, fraction 1.0) and pair_kernel_3.5 (endpoint_effects:11, z 0.540, q 9.8e-5, fraction 1.0), with pair_kernel_5.0 weaker (endpoint_effects:12, z 0.319, q 3.7e-3) and pair_kernel_7.0 opposite in sign (endpoint_effects:13, z -0.485, q 1.5e-4). The same ordering appears in the branch-adjusted covariance and correlation rows (branch_adjusted:86,87,163,164,240,241), so the short-range pair signal is not an artifact of one adjustment.

Descendant survival credit is much weaker and mostly unadjusted-significant: landmark_00_soft_mass (survival_effects:0, z 0.365, q 0.120), landmark_07_soft_mass (survival_effects:70, z 0.220, q 0.356), landmark_10_soft_mass (survival_effects:100, z 0.234, q 0.302) and landmark_18_local_czz (survival_effects:186, z 0.217, q 0.302) are the only positive survival rows with q below 0.5, while several negative rows (survival_effects:56, 96, 146, 156, 195) also fail q<0.05. Survival credit therefore does not reproduce the endpoint pair-kernel ranking and cannot be read as final affinity benefit.

The actual later-label calculation is unavailable: decoded_terminal_learning_labels_available is false, the label semantics are recorded affinities removed with an equal score prior, and lineage_support records terminal metadata at terminal_score_time 0.99 / terminal_state_time 1.0 outside the learning window [0.0,0.5]. Last-record joint-head credit is therefore not a decoded terminal affinity label, and the immediate-versus-descendant comparison cannot be closed with final affinity benefit.

Ancestral coverage is thin and survivor-biased: lineage_support reports 349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 with fewer than 6, out of 700 batch nodes, with only 14 complete-survival batches and 17-28 teachers per node. Survival enrichment is computed on this sparse, parent-debiased strata, so the weak survival positives (survival_effects:0, 70, 100, 186) are conditional on surviving lineages rather than on the full ancestral population.

Joint-motion diagnostics are the most reproducible negative signals: joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_internal_RMS_A are negative with q at or below 0.044 in raw covariance, adjusted covariance and both correlation variants (branch_adjusted:74,76,151,153,228,230,305,307), and same-sign batch fractions reach 0.93-1.0. This is evidence that larger joint innovation/internal spread is associated with lower favorable contrast, not evidence of a neural-module cause.

Shape and global-pose terms are not uniformly informative: shape_yy is negative and reproducible (branch_adjusted:158 raw correlation q 2.6e-3, branch_adjusted:235 adjusted correlation q 0.015), while global centroid x/y/z rows are null after adjustment (branch_adjusted:77,78,79) and shape_xy/xz/zz are inconsistent. Pair_kernel_7.0 flips sign between raw and adjusted correlation (branch_adjusted:167 vs 244), so the long-range kernel direction is not stable.

Regional enrichment separates local translation from shape: local_dy enrichment is positive and reproducible at landmarks 02, 06, 09, 14 and 18 (regional_effects:22,62,92,142,182, all q<=4.3e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0), whereas local_cyy is negative at nearly every landmark (regional_effects:5,15,75,85,105,125,135,165,175,195, q<=1.8e-3). The local_dy direction is a region-specific coordinate signal, not a global pose or shape effect.

Parent-edge contrast rates are dominated by negative local_cxx and local_cyy at landmarks 00, 01, 04, 07, 08, 10, 11, 12, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18 and 19 (regional_effects:404,405,414,415,444,445,474,475,484,485,504,505,524,525,534,535,554,555,564,565,574,575,584,585,594,595), with positive local_cxz at many of the same landmarks (regional_effects:408,418,438,448,458,478,488,508,518,528,538,558,568,578,598). This is a within-path contrast pattern, not a population composition statement.

Turnover residuals are large and positive for local_cxx and local_cyy at landmarks 00, 01, 04, 07, 08, 16, 17, 18 and 19 (turnover:14,17,47,98,134,224,227,254,257,497,524,527,584,587, q<=0.058, positive batch fraction 0.86-1.0), while the corresponding population rates are small or negative. The residual is an accounting diagnostic for reclassification and parent weighting, not a causal selection effect or atom velocity.

The supplied continuous contrast functions are observed-node linear interpolations on [0.0,0.49] with no extrapolation allowed, and they show sign changes and rate changes within the window: landmark_00_soft_mass rises then falls (continuous:0, first_z -0.366, last_z -0.275, 4 sign changes), landmark_00_local_dx and local_dy have large first-rate z (-17.5 and -72.4) that reverse sign by the last node (continuous:1,2), and landmark_00_local_cxx/cyy/czz are negative through most of the window (continuous:4,5,6). A constant rule is not supported by these curves; a time-conditioned rule would need validated fits, and curve_support shows relative node RMSE 0.29-0.93 with strong sign conflicts, so the curves are contrasts rather than absolute reward targets.

Parent-child increment contrasts are mostly not significant after multiplicity adjustment: shape_xx and shape_yy have negative success-failure integrated rates (increment_effects:3,4, q 0.095 and 0.161), shape_xz and pair_kernel_2.5 are positive (increment_effects:7,10, q 0.207 and 0.208), and landmark_00_softmin is negative (increment_effects:14, q 0.046) while landmark_00_occupancy3 is positive (increment_effects:15, q 0.081). The increment table therefore does not establish a within-path change that survives adjustment, and its residual accounting should not be read as a causal selection effect.

Joint diagnostics show that selection innovation is positively associated with native alignment and teacher innovation-contrast alignment (joint_diagnostics:1,11, q 2.2e-9, positive batch fraction 1.0) but negatively associated with observed child score gain (joint_diagnostics:2, q 1.8e-7, positive batch fraction 0.0), and teacher contrast is mostly internal (joint_diagnostics:14, internal fraction 0.787). The information audit further reports compressed-choice excess fixed RMS 0.081 A and chosen teacher score correlation 0.102, so the teacher signal is a coordinate contrast, not a validated affinity predictor.

hypotheses.claim: Hypothesis: a short-range pair-kernel coordinate intervention (pair_kernel_1.5-3.5) is the most testable direction, because it is the only endpoint family with q<1e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0 and consistent branch-adjusted covariance/correlation signs. Observable: pair_kernel_1.5/2.5/3.5 enrichment. Intended response: increased favorable-minus-comparison contrast at the endpoint. Target origin: endpoint pointcloud coordinates. Scale: 1.5-3.5 A pair-distance shells. Discriminating failure: if the endpoint pair-kernel contrast does not move while joint_innovation_RMS_A remains negative, the direction is not supported.

Hypothesis: a region-specific local_dy intervention at landmarks 02, 06, 09, 14 or 18 is testable, because local_dy enrichment is positive and reproducible there while local_cyy is negative at nearly all landmarks. Observable: local_dy enrichment at the chosen landmark. Intended response: increased favorable contrast without a global centroid shift. Target origin: landmark-centered regional moments. Scale: 5 A radius. Discriminating failure: if local_dy enrichment rises but global centroid or shape_yy also moves in the same direction, the effect is not region-specific.

Hypothesis: a time-conditioned regional attention rule using the validated absolute contrast changes at actual score nodes is testable, because the observed-node curves show sign changes and rate reversals within [0.0,0.49] (continuous:0-9) and curve_support reports relative node RMSE 0.29-0.93 with strong sign conflicts. Observable: the same regional contrast measured at early versus late score nodes. Intended response: a sign-consistent contrast change across the window. Target origin: static teacher coordinates with only validated absolute contrast changes. Scale: observed score times 0.0-0.49. Discriminating failure: if the contrast change is not reproducible across independent batches or requires extrapolation outside the observed support, the time-conditioned rule is not supported.

Hypothesis: the large positive turnover residuals for local_cxx/local_cyy at landmarks 00, 01, 04, 07, 08, 16, 17, 18 and 19 reflect changing cohort composition and parent weighting rather than within-path change, because the parent-child increment contrasts are mostly not significant after adjustment (increment_effects:3,4,7,10,14,15). Observable: turnover residual rate versus increment contrast rate for the same feature. Intended response: residual magnitude tracks reclassification and parent weighting, not a within-path coordinate change. Target origin: population and edge rate accounting. Scale: whole window [0.0,0.5]. Discriminating failure: if a significant within-path increment contrast appears for the same feature, the composition explanation is weakened.

Hypothesis: a teacher-neighbor or blend intervention is testable only as a coordinate contrast, because joint diagnostics show selection innovation aligns with teacher innovation contrast (joint_diagnostics:11) but negatively with observed child score gain (joint_diagnostics:2), and the information audit reports chosen teacher score correlation 0.102 with excess fixed RMS 0.081 A. Observable: teacher contrast coherence and observed child score gain. Intended response: increased teacher contrast coherence without a decrease in observed child score gain. Target origin: detached nearest-k teacher coordinates. Scale: teacher_neighbors 2-8 and blend 0.25-1.0. Discriminating failure: if teacher contrast coherence rises while observed child score gain falls further, the intervention is not supported as an affinity direction.

Hypothesis: joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_internal_RMS_A are the most reproducible negative diagnostics and can serve as a discriminating failure condition for any coordinate intervention, because they are negative with q<=0.044 and same-sign batch fractions 0.93-1.0 across raw, adjusted and correlation variants. Observable: joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_internal_RMS_A. Intended response: no increase in joint innovation/internal spread under a supported intervention. Target origin: joint geometry diagnostics. Scale: whole window [0.0,0.5]. Discriminating failure: if a proposed intervention increases joint innovation/internal spread while claiming favorable contrast, the direction is not supported.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity; decoded_terminal_learning_labels_available is false.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.
All weak and null scalar effects retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
The executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term; moment and pair-kernel effects are diagnostic only.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters and no temperature edit is proposed.
